procs.rm: Roundwood logs (eucalyptus, hardwood mix), bamboo (some plants)
procs.out: Screened wood chips (25-40mm) to digester
procs.q: Chip size distribution, bark%, dirt%, moisture%, fines%

loc: Screened chip conveyor to chip pile
Reclaimer to digester feed conveyor (final quality checkpoint)
d: Analyses overhead camera feeds and metal detectors at chip handling conveyors.
Detects oversize, fines, bark contamination, dirt and foreign material in chip stream.
Provides real-time chip quality feedback and triggers diverter action on foreign material.
p: Chip quality variability causes digester DP swings (critical for dissolving pulp)
uc.calc: Yield improvement 1% × wood cost ₹5,000/t × 2 t/t pulp = ₹100/t pulp = ₹10 cr/MTPA potential × 20-30% capture = ₹2-3 cr/MTPA.

d: Analyses chipper motor current, vibration on shaft bearings, and chip size analyzer data.
Detects knife dullness, breakage, anvil wear and bearing degradation.
Provides knife change scheduling and predicts maintenance windows before unplanned downtime.
p: Chip quality degrades silently before knife change
Manual inspection only at scheduled changes
kpi: Chip quality variance attributed to knife wear
uc.calc: Unplanned chipper downtime avoidance + chip quality stability. ₹1 cr per MTPA pulp.

loc: Chip pile reclaimer to digester feed trunk belt (single-point failure for pulping)
Foreign material detection at digester feed
d: Analyses camera images, vibration on idlers, and metal detector signals.
Detects belt tears, mis-tracking, foreign material and bearing degradation.
Provides location-tagged alerts before catastrophic belt failure or downstream damage.
p: Long wood yard conveyors fail with limited warning
Foreign material damages digester feed system
Digester feed line failure halts pulping (single-point)
Belt damage often noticed only on inspection rounds
uc.calc: Belt failure prevention + jam events avoided. ₹0.5 cr per MTPA pulp.

procs.rm: Wood chips, prehydrolysis liquor (water/steam), white liquor (NaOH + Na2S)
procs.out: Brown stock dissolving pulp (high alpha-cellulose), prehydrolysis effluent, weak black liquor
procs.q: Alpha-cellulose %, kappa number, DP (degree of polymerization), yield %, hemicellulose %

d: Analyses prehydrolysis liquor temperature, time, P-factor calculation, and dissolved hemicellulose data.
Models prehydrolysis kinetics and predicts hemicellulose removal efficiency.
Provides advisory on PHK temperature and time for target alpha-cellulose with minimum DP loss.
p: PHK is unique to dissolving pulp; operators rely on experience
Excessive PHK degrades DP; insufficient leaves hemicellulose
uc.calc: Alpha-cellulose uplift 1-2% reduces HAE load + improves yield. Steam savings from optimized PHK conditions. ₹4 cr per MTPA pulp.

d: Analyses chip-meter data, cooking liquor flow/temperature, H-factor calculation, and online kappa/DP analyzer data.
Models cooking kinetics specific to dissolving pulp (alpha-cellulose, DP target).
Provides real-time advisory on liquor charge, temperature and retention for target alpha-cellulose and DP.
p: Dissolving pulp DP must stay tight (affects fibre tenacity downstream)
Operators trade yield for DP conservatively
uc.calc: DP/alpha-cellulose stability + yield improvement 1-2% × wood cost + reduced bleach chemical demand downstream. ₹8 cr per MTPA pulp.

procs.rm: Brown stock dissolving pulp slurry, wash water (recycled hot)
procs.out: Washed brown stock pulp, weak black liquor to evaporators
procs.q: Wash loss (kg Na2SO4/ADt), dilution factor, soda losses

d: Analyses conductivity, dilution factor, drum speed and wash water flow on each washer stage.
Predicts wash efficiency and soda losses; identifies anomalies in drum loading.
Provides advisory on dilution factor and wash water distribution across stages.
uc.calc: Wash loss reduction 1-2 kg Na2SO4/ADt × ₹15/kg × 1 MTPA equivalent. ₹2 cr per MTPA pulp.

f: Brown stock pulp + O2 + NaOH + Mg salts
procs.rm: Brown stock pulp from washing, oxygen, NaOH, Mg salts (DP protector)
procs.ut: Oxygen (high pressure), NaOH solution, steam (temperature), power
procs.out: Delignified pulp (reduced kappa, alpha-cellulose uplifted), spent liquor to washing
procs.q: Kappa reduction %, alpha-cellulose %, DP preservation, brightness uplift

uc.t: Oxygen Delignification Chemical & DP Preservation Optimization
d: Analyses O2 dosage, NaOH charge, Mg salt addition, reactor temperature/pressure and resulting kappa reduction and DP preservation.
Models O2 delignification kinetics specific to dissolving pulp (lower kappa target + DP preservation tradeoff).
Provides O2, NaOH and temperature setpoint advisory for target kappa with minimum DP loss and minimum chemical cost.
p: O2 delignification cost balance is delicate (more O2/NaOH = more kappa drop but DP risk)
Mg salt dosing for DP protection often empirical
Lab feedback on kappa+DP slow (2-3 hr)
Manual chemical charging variable across shifts
Sub-optimal O2 delig pushes higher chemical cost to bleach plant downstream
uc.calc: Kappa reduction 30-50% via O2 delig × downstream ClO2 savings 15-20% × ₹180/kg × 25 kg/t = ₹0.7-1.2 cr/MTPA in bleach savings. Plus DP preservation enables better fibre tenacity. Plus NaOH + O2 dosing optimization at this stage. ₹4 cr per MTPA pulp.

procs.rm: Brown stock pulp, hot alkali (NaOH solution)
procs.ut: MP steam (alkali heating), power, NaOH makeup
procs.out: HAE-treated pulp (reduced hemicellulose), HAE effluent
procs.q: Residual hemicellulose %, alpha-cellulose uplift, DP preservation, NaOH consumption

d: Analyses HAE tower temperature, retention time, alkali charge, and downstream hemicellulose results.
Models HAE kinetics and predicts hemicellulose removal versus alkali consumption.
Provides setpoint advisory for target hemicellulose with minimum NaOH usage and DP preservation.
p: HAE NaOH consumption is significant cost
DP loss during HAE is a real risk
uc.calc: NaOH savings 30-50 kg/t pulp × ₹35/kg = ₹1-2,000/t pulp = ₹10-20 cr/MTPA × 25-30% capture = ₹3-6 cr/MTPA pulp.

procs.rm: HAE pulp, ClO2, O2, H2O2, NaOH, H2SO4 (for pH adjustment)
procs.out: Bleached dissolving pulp (high brightness, controlled DP)
procs.q: Brightness (ISO%), DP (degree of polymerization), viscosity, alpha-cellulose%

uc.t: Bleach Plant Chemical & DP Preservation Optimization
d: Analyses incoming pulp DP and brightness, ClO2 dosage per stage, alkali dosage, tower temperatures and retention.
Models bleaching kinetics for dissolving grade (preserving DP is critical, unlike paper grade).
Provides setpoint optimization for chemical charge to hit target brightness with minimum DP loss and minimum chemicals.
p: Dissolving pulp requires careful bleach (cannot over-bleach or DP drops)
Lab DP/brightness lag prevents real-time control
Operators over-bleach for brightness safety margin
DP loss in bleach hurts downstream fibre tenacity
uc.calc: ClO2 reduction 5-10% × 25 kg/t × ₹180/kg × 1 MTPA equivalent = ₹2-5 cr. Plus DP preservation enables higher fibre tenacity (premium grade pricing). ₹10 cr per MTPA pulp.

uc.t: Dissolving Pulp Strength & DP Inferential Modeling
d: Analyses incoming pulp quality, bleaching conditions and lab DP/brightness measurements.
Builds soft sensors for DP and brightness between lab samples (typically every 2-4 hours).
Provides real-time quality predictions enabling faster control loops.
p: Lab DP measurement is the binding constraint on bleach control
DP drift only caught after off-spec
Control loops too slow to respond
uc.calc: Faster control + reduced off-spec lots. ₹3 cr per MTPA pulp.

procs.rm: Bleached wet pulp (~50% solids from press)
procs.out: Air-dry baled dissolving pulp (~92-95% solids) or wet pulp to viscose
procs.q: Moisture%, sheet uniformity, bale weight, surface defects

d: Analyses dryer cylinder pressures, condensate flows, sheet moisture profile and surface temperatures.
Models drying kinetics and predicts moisture profile versus steam distribution and speed.
Provides advisory on steam group setpoints for target moisture with minimum steam consumption.
p: Drying is largest steam consumer at pulp end
uc.calc: Steam savings 2-3% on pulp dryer steam. ₹4 cr per MTPA pulp.

d: Analyses camera feeds of dried pulp sheet at the sheeter and baler.
Detects sheet breaks, edge defects, basis weight anomalies, dirt specks and surface marks.
Provides quality classification and rejects bad bales before storage/dispatch.
p: Bale defects discovered at customer or downstream viscose
Sheet breaks at sheeter cause production loss
Customer audits frequent for dissolving pulp grade
uc.calc: Reject reduction + customer complaint reduction. ₹1.5 cr per MTPA pulp.

procs.rm: Dissolving pulp sheets (or wet pulp), steeping NaOH (17-19% w/w)
procs.out: Alkali cellulose (shredded), steeping liquor (recycled), press lye
procs.q: Alkali cellulose composition (cellulose II, NaOH content), shredded particle size

d: Analyses steeping NaOH concentration, temperature, pulp throughput, and alkali cellulose properties (cellulose II content, NaOH retention).
Models steeping kinetics and predicts alkali cellulose quality at target NaOH consumption.
Provides advisory on NaOH concentration, temperature and retention time for consistent alkali cellulose at minimum NaOH usage.
p: Steeping NaOH cost is significant (₹2,000/t fibre equivalent)
Alkali cellulose quality variability impacts downstream xanthation
Operators over-charge NaOH for safety margin
uc.calc: NaOH savings 3-5% × 700 kg/t fibre × ₹35/kg × 1 MTPA = ₹7-12 cr/MTPA × 50% capture = ₹4-6 cr/MTPA fibre.

d: Analyses press load, press lye flow, shredder motor current, and alkali cellulose particle size distribution.
Detects press performance degradation, shredder wear, and alkali cellulose quality issues.
Provides press setpoint advisory and shredder change scheduling.
p: Alkali cellulose particle size affects xanthation
uc.calc: Press lye recovery + shredder maintenance. ₹2 cr per MTPA fibre.

f: Aging drums / conveyors (controlled time + temp + O2)
procs.rm: Alkali cellulose (shredded)
procs.ut: Controlled atmosphere (O2 in some processes), power for conveyors
procs.out: Aged alkali cellulose (target DP for spinning)
procs.q: DP (degree of polymerization) target, aging uniformity, particle size

d: Analyses aging drum/conveyor temperature, retention time, oxygen exposure and resulting alkali cellulose DP.
Models aging kinetics (oxidative depolymerization) and predicts target DP for downstream spinning.
Provides aging condition advisory to hit DP target consistently.
p: DP control through aging is delicate (overshooting reduces fibre tenacity)
uc.calc: DP consistency + fibre tenacity improvement. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Aged alkali cellulose, CS2 (carbon disulphide), NaOH solution
procs.ut: Power (xanthator drums), CS2 (recovered + makeup), cooling water
procs.out: Cellulose xanthate (orange/yellow), excess CS2 (recovered), H2S byproduct
procs.q: Xanthate gamma value (degree of substitution), CS2 conversion %, residual CS2

d: Analyses CS2 dosage, xanthator temperature, reaction time, alkali cellulose properties, and xanthate gamma value at outlet.
Models xanthation kinetics and predicts gamma value versus CS2 consumption and reaction conditions.
Provides CS2 dosage advisory for target gamma at minimum fresh CS2 consumption.
p: CS2 is the most expensive variable input (₹120/kg, 50-100 kg/t fibre net)
CS2 dosage often conservative (excess for safety)
CS2 losses to recovery system high
uc.calc: CS2 reduction 5-7% × 75 kg/t fibre × ₹120/kg × 1 MTPA = ₹4.5-6.3 cr × scaling = ₹8 cr per MTPA fibre (with feedback effects on recovery).

procs.rm: Cellulose xanthate, dilute NaOH solution
procs.out: Viscose solution (cellulose xanthate dissolved in dilute caustic)
procs.q: Viscose viscosity, gamma value, ripeness index (Hottenroth/salt test), filterability

d: Analyses dissolution tank conditions, ripening time and temperature, lab Hottenroth/salt test data, and viscosity measurements.
Models viscose ripening kinetics and predicts spinnability indicators.
Provides ripening setpoint advisory to hit target viscose properties for spinning.
p: Ripening time is critical (under-ripe or over-ripe disrupts spinning)
Manual ripening time setting per batch
uc.calc: Spinnability improvement reduces fibre defects and breaks at spinneret. ₹5 cr per MTPA fibre.

d: Analyses dissolution tank temperatures, cooling water flow and dissolution mixer power.
Models dissolution kinetics and predicts viscose quality versus operating conditions.
Provides cooling and mixing setpoint advisory for consistent viscose with minimum utility consumption.
uc.calc: Utility savings + quality consistency. ₹2 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Viscose solution
procs.out: Filtered, deaerated viscose ready for spinning
procs.q: Filter pressure drop, deaeration vacuum, filtration value

d: Analyses filter pressure drop trends, filter media life, deaeration vacuum and bubble content.
Predicts filter clogging and recommends cleaning/change intervals.
Provides filtration and deaeration setpoint advisory for consistent spinning feed.
p: Vacuum issues hidden until quality drops
kpi: Spinning rejection rate from feed quality
uc.calc: Spinning quality improvement + reduced filter media cost. ₹2 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Filtered viscose, spin bath (H2SO4 + Na2SO4 + ZnSO4 solution)
procs.out: Wet regenerated cellulose tow (fibre tow before stretching)
procs.q: Spin bath composition, tow stability, spinneret performance, fibre denier

uc.t: Spin Bath Chemistry Optimization (H2SO4, ZnSO4, Na2SO4)
d: Analyses spin bath composition (online or frequent lab data), spinning quality, fibre properties and spin bath circulation.
Models regeneration kinetics and predicts fibre properties versus bath composition.
Provides bath composition advisory and ZnSO4/H2SO4 makeup setpoints for target fibre quality at minimum chemical cost.
p: Spin bath composition control is delicate and affects fibre quality
Composition variability causes fibre property swings
uc.calc: ZnSO4 cost reduction 5-10% + H2SO4 optimization + fibre quality uplift. ₹5 cr per MTPA fibre.

d: Analyses spinning conditions (bath chemistry, jet velocity, stretch ratio), tow tension and lab fibre property results.
Builds inferential model for fibre tenacity, elongation and denier between lab samples.
Provides spinning advisory to hit premium fibre property grades consistently.
p: Premium fibre grades (high tenacity) earn ₹5-10/kg premium
Operators run mid-grade settings to avoid off-spec risk
Customer audits frequent for premium grades
uc.calc: Premium grade share increase 5-10% × ₹5-10/kg premium × 1 MTPA = ₹5-10 cr. ₹7 cr per MTPA fibre.

d: Analyses spinneret pressure drop trends, fibre quality correlation per spinneret, and CV inspection of spinneret faces during cleaning.
Detects spinneret clogging, hole damage, and cleaning effectiveness.
Provides spinneret cleaning schedule and replacement advisory.
p: Spinneret damage hidden until quality drop
uc.calc: Spinneret life extension + reduced cleaning + fibre quality. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Wet regenerated tow
procs.out: Cut staple fibre (32-38mm typical)
procs.q: Fibre tenacity, elongation, denier, length variation, defects

d: Analyses godet speeds, stretch ratios, plasticization bath conditions and fibre tension profiles.
Models stretching effect on fibre orientation and mechanical properties.
Provides godet speed and stretch ratio setpoint advisory for target fibre properties.
uc.calc: Tenacity uplift + reduced tow breaks. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Cut wet staple fibre (acidic, contains Na2SO4, residual chemicals)
procs.out: Washed fibre (low Na2SO4, neutral pH), wash effluent to recovery
procs.q: Residual Na2SO4 %, residual H2SO4, fibre pH, wash efficiency

d: Analyses wash water flow, counter-current washer stage conductivity, residual sulphate and acid in fibre.
Models washing kinetics and predicts residual chemical removal versus water consumption.
Provides water distribution and washer setpoint advisory for minimum water with target wash efficiency.
p: Fibre washing is water-intensive (5-10 m³/t fibre)
Residual chemicals affect fibre quality and ETP load
uc.calc: Fresh water reduction + reduced ETP load + Na2SO4 recovery uplift. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Washed fibre, finish (soft finish oil)
procs.out: Dry crimped staple fibre ready for baling
procs.q: Moisture %, crimp count/cm, finish %, fibre tenacity, denier consistency

d: Analyses belt dryer zone temperatures, residence time, fibre moisture and exit quality.
Models drying kinetics and predicts exit moisture and fibre quality versus dryer conditions.
Provides zone setpoint advisory for target moisture with minimum energy.
p: Fibre drying is the largest energy consumer at fibre end
Moisture variability affects baling and customer quality
uc.calc: Energy savings 5-8% × ₹50-80 cr/MTPA fibre drying energy. ₹5 cr per MTPA fibre.

d: Analyses camera feeds of crimped fibre at the crimper exit and finish application.
Detects crimp irregularities, finish overdose/underdose, and surface defects.
Provides crimper and finish line setpoint advisory.
p: Crimp variability affects downstream spinnability at customer
uc.calc: Customer reject reduction + finish oil savings. ₹2 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: CS2-laden gases from xanthation, dissolution, spin bath, fibre processing areas
procs.ut: Power (compressors, ID fans), absorbent media (activated carbon), steam (regeneration)
procs.out: Recovered CS2 returned to xanthation, residual emissions to scrubber
procs.q: CS2 recovery efficiency %, fresh CS2 makeup rate (kg/t fibre), CS2 emission rate

d: Analyses CS2 capture system performance (vapor capture efficiency, condenser performance, activated carbon bed cycling), CS2 emission monitor data, and process areas inventory.
Models CS2 mass balance plant-wide and identifies losses by area (xanthation, dissolution, spin bath, fibre processing).
Provides location-specific advisory on capture system operations and recovery sequence optimization.
p: CS2 is the single largest variable cost (₹600-900 cr/MTPA fibre gross)
Recovery efficiency 85-90% typical; lifting to 92-95% is huge
Capture system performance not real-time monitored
Operators rely on lab CS2 measurements
CS2 emission compliance + financial stake aligned
uc.calc: Recovery improvement 2-4 percentage points × 75 kg/t × ₹120/kg × 1 MTPA = ₹18-36 cr potential × 50-70% capture = ₹10-25 cr/MTPA. ₹20 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: H2S byproduct from xanthation and recovery loops
procs.out: Captured sulfide for sulphuric acid production, cleaned gas to stack
procs.q: H2S concentration in exit gas, capture efficiency %, S compound recovery

d: Analyses H2S concentration in source gases, caustic scrubber performance, sulphide solution quality, and downstream H2SO4 production efficiency.
Models H2S capture and conversion to H2SO4; predicts plant-wide sulphur balance.
Provides advisory on scrubber and Claus/wet process operation for maximum sulphur recovery and compliant emissions.
p: Sulphur recovery imperfect (waste of source material)
kpi: H2SO4 production from byproduct (% of plant demand)
uc.calc: Caustic savings + H2SO4 production uplift + compliance margin. ₹4 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Used spin bath (H2SO4, Na2SO4, ZnSO4, dissolved cellulose impurities)
procs.ut: Power (pumps, filters), fresh H2SO4 / ZnSO4 makeup
procs.out: Regenerated spin bath returned to spinning line, Na2SO4 byproduct to crystallizer
procs.q: H2SO4 strength, Na2SO4 level, ZnSO4 level, impurity levels

d: Analyses used spin bath quality, regeneration system performance (filtration, concentration), and makeup chemical consumption.
Models bath chemistry over recycling cycles and predicts makeup needs.
Provides regeneration setpoint advisory for minimum makeup with consistent spinning bath quality.
p: ZnSO4 makeup cost high (zinc price volatile)
uc.calc: ZnSO4 + H2SO4 makeup reduction. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

d: Analyses zinc inventory in spin bath, fibre carryover, and crystallization fractionation.
Predicts ZnSO4 losses and recovery opportunities.
Provides recovery setpoint advisory to minimize zinc losses.
p: Zinc inventory not tracked in real-time
uc.calc: Zinc loss reduction × LME zinc price. ₹2 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Na2SO4-rich liquor from spin bath regeneration and fibre washing
procs.out: Crystallized Na2SO4 byproduct (saleable glauber salt or anhydrous), mother liquor
procs.q: Na2SO4 purity (>99%), particle size, moisture, salable grade compliance

d: Analyses crystallizer feed quality, evaporator performance, crystallization conditions, centrifuge output and crystal product quality.
Models crystallization kinetics and predicts product yield and quality.
Provides crystallizer setpoint advisory for maximum byproduct yield and quality compliance.
p: Na2SO4 byproduct is significant revenue (~₹5-8/kg × 300 kg/t fibre)
uc.calc: Yield improvement 3-5% + quality uplift for premium pricing. ₹4 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Press lye, dilute NaOH from various process streams
procs.out: Concentrated NaOH for reuse in steeping, residual stream
procs.q: NaOH strength (g/L), purity, recovered volume vs makeup

d: Analyses dilute NaOH feed flow, evaporator performance, and concentrated NaOH output quality.
Predicts recovery efficiency and steam consumption versus operating conditions.
Provides evaporator setpoint advisory for maximum recovery at minimum steam.
p: NaOH makeup is significant ongoing cost
uc.calc: Recovery improvement + steam optimization. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Coal, biomass (bark/sludge), makeup water
procs.out: HP steam, flue gas, ash
procs.q: Steam generation rate, boiler efficiency %, O2/CO/NOx, ash carbon%

d: Analyses fuel firing rate, air distribution, flue gas O2/CO/NOx, steam generation and ash carbon.
Models combustion versus fuel mix and predicts boiler efficiency, emissions and ash quality.
Provides air, fuel and load setpoint advisory for maximum steam at minimum fuel within emission limits.
uc.calc: Fuel savings 2-4% on ₹100-150 cr fuel cost. ₹5 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: HP/MP/LP steam from power boiler and recovery systems
procs.out: Steam delivered to digesters, bleach plant, evaporators, fibre dryer
procs.q: Header pressures, flow distribution, condensate recovery%, venting losses

d: Analyses steam flows, pressures and consumption across plant (boiler, digesters, bleach plant, evaporators, dryers).
Models steam balance and identifies inefficient consumers and venting losses.
Provides plant-wide optimization advisory.
uc.calc: Network optimization 2-3% on total steam value. ₹5 cr per MTPA fibre.

loc: HP/MP/LP steam header drip legs (prevent water hammer)
Pulp dryer cylinder drains (large area, frequent failures)
Distribution and tracing line drainage points across the plant
d: Analyses inlet and outlet temperature signatures from wireless battery-powered sensors deployed at each steam trap.
Detects failed-open (steam passing), failed-closed (condensate backup), and failed-cold (dead) conditions using temperature delta logic.
Provides location-tagged alerts to maintenance, replacing annual audit cycles with continuous monitoring.
p: 10-25% of steam traps fail at any time
Annual ultrasonic audits miss interim failures
Failed-open traps waste ₹2-25 lakh per trap per year
No continuous monitoring at scale (plant has 1,500-3,000 traps)
Manual inspection cannot cover full population
uc.calc: Trap failure rate 15% × 2,000 traps × ₹4 lakh/yr × 50% capture = ₹6 cr/yr at 0.5 MTPA = ₹12 cr/MTPA gross. Net ₹4 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Combined plant effluent (acidic, alkaline, sulphate-rich, BOD/COD load)
procs.ut: Power (aerators, pumps), chemicals (pH correction, polymer), nutrients
procs.out: Treated effluent, biological sludge
procs.q: Inlet/outlet BOD, COD, TSS, sulphate, pH, DO, MLSS

d: Analyses inlet effluent characteristics (BOD, COD, TSS, sulphate, pH), aeration tank DO, MLSS, RAS flow and outlet quality.
Models biological treatment kinetics and predicts outlet compliance margins.
Provides aeration, RAS and chemical dosing advisory for compliance and energy minimization.
p: VSF effluent is sulphate-rich and complex
uc.calc: Aeration savings + compliance + chemical optimization. ₹4 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Raw water (river/bore), treated effluent (recycle)
procs.ut: Power (pumps), chemicals (alum, polymer, antiscalant), filtration media
procs.out: Fresh water for process, recycled water for non-critical uses
procs.q: Turbidity, hardness, conductivity, microbiological load, reuse ratio

d: Analyses raw water characteristics, treated water quality and reuse loop quality.
Predicts filter cleaning needs, dosing requirements and reuse opportunities.
Provides setpoint advisory to maximize reuse and minimize fresh water intake.
p: VSF is extremely water-intensive (50-100 m³/t fibre)
uc.calc: Fresh water reduction + reuse uplift. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Atmospheric air
procs.out: Compressed air for pneumatic actuators, instruments, conveying
procs.q: Network pressure (bar), flow (Nm3/h), dew point, leak rate %

d: Analyses compressor load, network pressure, flow at consumers and leak rates.
Detects compressor cycling, network leaks and pressure drops.
Provides advisory on compressor sequencing, network repairs and pressure setpoints.
uc.calc: Leak reduction + sequencing. ₹1 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: OT data (DCS/PLC), MES, ERP, lab/LIMS data, IoT sensor streams
procs.ut: Edge gateways, network infrastructure, cloud compute, storage
procs.out: Unified data layer enabling all AI use cases
procs.q: Tag coverage %, data quality, latency, uptime, governance compliance

uc.vt: Enabler for all other use cases
d: Foundational data layer: unified namespace, historian access, MES integration, ERP linkage.
Enables every other AI use case by providing reliable, tagged, contextual data.
Provides time-series storage, governance, role-based access and edge-to-cloud connectivity.
p: Plant data scattered across DCS, PLC, lab, ERP
Analytics projects start with data plumbing every time
uc.calc: Enabler — value realized through downstream use cases.

procs.rm: Lab samples, online quality sensors, customer specs, regulatory limits
procs.ut: Lab instruments, LIMS infrastructure, calibration standards
procs.out: Quality intelligence dashboards, certificates of analysis, traceability records
procs.q: Spec compliance %, lab turnaround time, COA accuracy, customer complaints

d: Integrates lab quality data (digester DP, alpha-cellulose, brightness, gamma value, ripeness, fibre tenacity) with online process data.
Builds quality intelligence dashboards, SPC charts and root cause analysis.
Provides early warning on quality drift and faster lab-to-process feedback loops.
p: VSF has many lab parameters (DP, alpha, gamma, ripeness, tenacity)
uc.calc: Quality drift reduction + off-spec production reduction. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: Sensor data, maintenance history, spare parts data
procs.ut: Edge processing, CBM platform, CMMS software, MRO inventory system
procs.out: Failure predictions, work orders, reliability KPIs, optimized spares
procs.q: Equipment availability %, MTBF, MTTR, maintenance cost/t fibre, unplanned downtime hours

d: Analyses vibration, temperature, oil quality and motor signature data from critical rotating equipment (xanthator drums, dissolvers, spinning godets, dryers, agitators, pumps, blowers).
Predicts bearing failures, alignment issues, lubrication problems and impending breakdowns.
Provides location-tagged alerts and remaining-useful-life estimates.
p: Unplanned trips on spinning line cause major broke
uc.calc: Unplanned downtime reduction × fibre margin × hours saved. ₹15 cr per MTPA fibre.

d: Workflow management for maintenance work orders, planned/unplanned tracking, asset history and maintenance KPIs.
Integrates CBM alerts into work order generation and tracks closure.
Provides asset-level reliability metrics (MTBF, MTTR), maintenance cost reporting and compliance audit trails.
p: Work orders don't close on time
uc.calc: Work order closure reduction + maintenance cost transparency. ₹5 cr per MTPA fibre.

d: Analyses spare parts inventory, lead times, criticality, consumption patterns and supplier reliability.
Models optimal stocking levels, reorder points and consignment opportunities for critical spares.
Provides inventory optimization advisory and supplier performance dashboards.
uc.calc: Inventory reduction 15-25% + emergency procurement savings. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: CCTV feeds, gas detection (CS2, H2S, H2SO4 mist), access control, incident history
procs.ut: CV platform, edge inference, SCM integration, alert infrastructure
procs.out: Real-time safety alerts, compliance reports, near-miss analytics
procs.q: PPE compliance %, restricted-zone violations, CS2 exposure events, near-misses

d: Critical zones: xanthation area (CS2 exposure), viscose dissolution, spinning area (H2SO4 mist + CS2), chemical handling, recovery systems.
Analyses CCTV feeds with computer vision (PPE compliance, restricted-zone intrusion) integrated with CS2 and H2S gas detection data.
Provides real-time alerts to control room and safety officers; integrates with site SCM.
p: CS2 exposure has serious health effects (neurological)
uc.calc: Incident avoidance + insurance + compliance audit. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

procs.rm: All plant data
procs.ut: Cloud compute, BI platform, scheduling engine
procs.out: Plant-wide OEE, KPI dashboards, schedule optimization, what-if scenarios
procs.q: OEE%, throughput, conversion cost (₹/t fibre), schedule adherence, grade mix margin

d: Integrates production, quality, energy and downtime data across all sections into role-based dashboards.
Provides automated OEE, specific energy and conversion-cost calculation; root cause analysis tools.
Enables data-driven decision making at all levels.
uc.calc: Systemic OEE + energy KPI tracking. ₹3 cr per MTPA fibre.

d: Analyses order book, fibre grade requirements (denier, length, finish), changeover times, and grade-specific economics.
Models grade campaign sequencing and predicts margin per scenario.
